entries.title: Genesis 20:1
segments: From thence; the groves of Hebron, where he had for some time resided.
Gerar; a city of the Philistines, south-east of Gaza.

entries.title: Genesis 20:2
segments: The best of men are entirely dependent for perseverance in holiness, for integrity, uprightness, and even external morality, upon the grace of God.  If left to themselves they will distrust Jehovah, give way to temptation, commit sin, and bring disgrace on religion, and distress, if not destruction, on themselves and others.

entries.title: Genesis 20:3
segments:
A dead man; he would be, should he not return Sarah to her husband. 
 
Before men had the Bible to guide them, God often made known his will in dreams: but now we have no reason to expect a revelation of his will in this way, as all needful directions in duty may be obtained from prayerful study of the Scriptures.

entries.title: Genesis 20:4
segments: A righteous nation; that is, me and my nation, which will be involved in my destruction, though we are guilty of no intentional wrong.

entries.title: Genesis 20:7
segments:
Shalt surely die; this shows God's abhorrence of the crime of adultery, and his indignation against those who commit it. 
 
Adultery is a sin which exposes all who commit it to the wrath of God, both in this world and in the world to come.

entries.title: Genesis 20:9
segments: Brought on me and on my kingdom; exposed us to commit a great sin.

entries.title: Genesis 20:12
segments: Not--of my mother; Terah, Abraham's father, is supposed by many interpreters to have had two wives; Haran, Sarah's father, to have been a son of the second; so that Sarah was his niece, and grandaughter of his father, but not of his mother.  The term sister was then often given to a niece, and brother to a nephew, uncle, or near relative,
; yet this use of these terms, in this case, was designed to deceive, and was wrong.

entries.title: Genesis 20:13
segments: The guilt of sin is greatly increased when it is made a part of a settled plan, or committed with forethought, deliberation, and fixed purpose; and were it not for the boundless grace of God, those who so sin would never be brought to repentance, but would inevitably perish.

entries.title: Genesis 20:16
segments:
A covering of the eyes--all other; words of difficult interpretation.  According to our version they seem to mean, Acknowledge thy brother (with allusion to Abraham's excuse) as thy husband.  Then he will be to thee a covering of the eyes to all men of thy company, and with all others; that is, will protect thee from their unlawful gaze, and from all harm.  But some prefer to render, Behold, it (the gift) shall be to thee a covering of the eyes; that is, an honorable atonement, so called because it leads the injured party, and all concerned, to overlook the injury received. 
 
The conduct of worldly men is often a reproof to professed Christians; such as ought to make them ashamed, and arouse them to greater confidence in God and greater devotion to his service.
